title: Hackers exploited iOS and Android flaws to infect phones
gist: Security firm Sekoia attributes with moderate-to-high confidence to Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service (APT29) a watering-hole campaign that used proxied sites impersonating america250.org and London's Raffles OWO hotel, plus a compromised Ukrainian web analytics service, to deliver zero-click iOS and Android exploit chains including DarkSword. All exploited flaws were already patched n-days, so only outdated devices were vulnerable.

insights.claim: Sekoia assessed with moderate to high confidence that Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service, tracked as APT29, ran a campaign injecting JavaScript into potentially hundreds of websites to profile iPhone and Android visitors and deliver tailored payloads stealing cookies, Wi-Fi passwords and full device data.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: State-backed mobile espionage at scale keeps demand high for mobile threat defense and device management.

insights.claim: Attackers registered america250[.]holiday as a reverse proxy to america250.org, the US 250th-anniversary site, and theowo[.]club to proxy London's Raffles OWO hotel near the Ministry of Defence and 10 Downing Street, where Volodymyr Zelenskyy reportedly stayed on October 14.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Targeting of diplomats and high-profile guests shows hospitality and event sites as espionage vectors.

insights.claim: The campaign used three infection vectors: direct JavaScript injection into legitimate site traffic, proxy domains, and a supply-chain compromise of a Ukrainian web analytics service serving thousands of sites, along with a compromised top Ukrainian gas producer's website.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Third-party script providers are a high-leverage attack surface, supporting web supply-chain security spending.

insights.claim: One of three zero-click exploit chains used was DarkSword, an iOS exploit kit that Google researchers say has been used by customers of Turkish commercial surveillance vendor PARS Defense and at least two other threat actors.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Commercial spyware tools are proliferating to state actors, raising regulatory scrutiny of the surveillance-vendor market.
insights.locator: One of the chains was DarkSword

insights.claim: All vulnerabilities exploited were n-days already patched by vendors, so the attacks only succeeded against outdated versions of iOS or Android.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Patch latency, not unknown flaws, is the main exposure, underscoring the value of update enforcement for enterprises.
